Is there any pair programming software for Linux users? Preferably one that has inter-OS functionality, i.e. that works with Linux, Windows, and Mac.

A couple that I've looked at:

  • Team Viewer - Let's you take full control of a user's computer. That way you can be looking at the same desktop and trade off who is in control. It's basically a very user friendly VPN solution. Free for personal use and available on Linux, Windows, Mac, Android and iOS. (And they might have a web viewer for ChromeOS.
  • Gobby - A programming editor that uses a shared server to send edits to all participants. Works a lot like when you're using Google Docs with more than one person at a time. Not a very powerful editor though so kind of pulls you out of your usual environment. Has binaries for Windows and Linux.

Don't use:

  • floobits - I don't know about other people's experience, but floobits seems to work great ... until it completely corrupts all of your source and you have to delete everything and reclone the repository to fix it. I don't know how common that is, but even the co-founder of Floobits says on their front page “Floobits works pretty well most of the time.” It's that time when it doesn't work that really screws you over.

It's a bit old school but you can use Screen on the linux box. Then putty from the windows box or ssh from the mac. Of course this is entirely terminal based - i.e. you'll need something like VIM + shell as your IDE which is a huge learning curve if you don't both already know it. For a more GUI centred approach then I second /u/d23's suggestion of tmux (although I use wmii as my tiling windows manager of choice).
